title: Cathedral of Santo Domingo
geometryBasis: Exact eight mapped footprint vertices and the two mapped enclosure walls. The 45.8 m rectangular nave, 54.6 m structural church length and octagonal presbytery follow the architectural survey. The 1899 north portal and clock stage and the 1915 plate of the older west front establish the two public elevations.
sectionBasis: The published RTK survey gives the seven bays, the 9.63 m central nave, 4.80 m aisles and relationships among vault heights. The clock documented in 1899 survived until its later relocation. Roof pitches, chapter room alignment, rose opening detail and external chapel profiles are bounded estimates.
limitations: The preserved mapped enclosure controls the outer shape. The 1899 appearance uses the Qualla north photograph, with the surviving west front corroborated by a published 1915 photograph.
The historic clock tower, external chapel roof pitches, exact portal locations and floor heights are approximate. The nineteenth-century clock mechanism is simplified.
Interior geometry depicts the load-bearing nave, aisles and ribbed vaults with simplified chapel partitions. Furnishings, tombs, stained-glass art and carved relief figures are outside the model.
The original modern elevation source remains unchanged and is used as an estimate for the historical grade.
